decisions.decision: How should weekly demand data be processed?
decisions.context: The retailer publishes forecasts weekly per store and product. Batch processing aligns the workflow with that cadence. [d:15]
decisions.rationale: A weekly batch run matches the stated forecast cadence and allows the team to rerun a past week against versioned inputs. [d:15, v:15.1]
consequences: Forecasts update on the scheduled run.
Historical runs need their input versions retained.

decisions.decision: How should model building and training run?
decisions.context: New model ideas should reach production quickly without disrupting the weekly run. An automated build pipeline can handle training, evaluation, and validation. [d:18, v:18.1]
decisions.rationale: An automated pipeline creates a repeatable route for training, evaluation, and validation, making it easier to advance model ideas without modifying the weekly forecast run directly. [d:18, v:18.1]
consequences: Model changes pass through the pipeline before release.
The team maintains pipeline definitions and evaluation steps.

decisions.context: Forecasting runs weekly, while the brief asks for reproducibility of any past week. Batch training supports versioned training runs tied to retained data. [d:19, v:19.1]
decisions.rationale: Offline batch training fits the weekly workflow and simplifies rerunning training from a specific historical data version. [d:19, v:19.1]
consequences: Training occurs on a scheduled batch.
Each run must record its data and model inputs.

decisions.decision: How should training data be versioned?
decisions.context: Reproducing forecasts for any past week requires identifying the data used in that run. The design space includes a dedicated data version repository. [d:11, v:11.1]
decisions.rationale: An explicit data version repository gives each historical run a stable data reference, which is central to the reproducibility requirement. [d:11, v:11.1]
consequences: Retain data versions for the required history.
Record the selected data version with each forecast run.

decisions.decision: How should the forecast pipeline be triggered?
decisions.context: The system produces weekly forecasts, so it needs a recurring trigger. The design space includes scheduled execution. [d:12, v:12.3]

alternatives.label: On-demand trigger
cons: Weekly run depends on manual action

decisions.rationale: A schedule provides the regular weekly execution the brief requires; ad hoc reruns can still be initiated as needed. [d:12, v:12.3]
consequences: The schedule and run status need operational ownership.
Past weeks can be rerun on demand.

decisions.decision: What should CI/CD build and deploy?
decisions.context: New model ideas must move quickly while protecting the weekly run. Automating model and system component delivery supports a repeatable release path. [d:25, v:25.1]

alternatives.label: Build, test, and deploy models to be served and other system components
Build, test, and deploy machine learning pipelines and components needed during pipeline runs
cons: Does not by itself automate model release

chosen.label: Build, test, and deploy models to be served and other system components

decisions.rationale: Automating model delivery gives the team a faster, repeatable route to production while preserving a controlled release step before the weekly run uses a new model. [d:25, v:25.1]
consequences: Release checks should complete before production use.

decisions.decision: How should a production model be replaced safely?
decisions.context: New models need to reach production without breaking the recurring forecast run. Keeping a rollback path supports recovery if a release causes problems. [d:10, v:10.2]
decisions.rationale: A rollback option provides a direct recovery path if a new model disrupts forecasting, supporting continuity of the weekly run. [d:10, v:10.2]
consequences: Keep the prior model version deployable.
Define how a failed release is detected and reversed.

decisions.decision: How should production model performance be monitored?
decisions.context: The weekly run must remain dependable as new models are introduced. Monitoring model performance can reveal degradation that warrants investigation or rollback. [d:22, v:22.1]

alternatives.label: Monitoring or logging data and predictions
cons: Logs alone do not assess model quality

decisions.rationale: Performance monitoring directly supports checking whether released models continue to produce acceptable forecasts across weekly runs. [d:22, v:22.1]
consequences: Choose forecast quality measures and review thresholds.
Monitoring results require an operational response.

uncovered: Forecast error metrics, acceptance thresholds, and promotion gates.
Forecast storage, delivery, and consumer interface.
Retention period and exact mechanism for historical input snapshots.
